name: Baby Bottle
baseMeaning: A baby bottle with a nipple, often depicted with milk inside.
tldr: 🍼 means baby bottles are ready, often serving as a soft hint that someone is expecting.

contextMeanings.meaning: It can simply stand for a baby bottle, milk, or the equipment used to feed an infant.
contextMeanings.example: we finally packed the spare 🍼 for the trip

contextMeanings.meaning: In an expecting announcement, it means the baby supplies are ready and something is coming soon.
It can jokingly describe a situation as needing baby-level care or preparation.
contextMeanings.example: this reunion needs a 🍼 and a timeout

contextMeanings.meaning: It may refer literally to bottles at a baby shower or workplace event without announcing a pregnancy.
contextMeanings.example: the office baby shower table has 🍼 on it

platformNotes.note: In a caption or comment, 🍼 works well as a soft expecting hint. Adding 👶 or a due date makes the announcement clearer when the message is separated from its context.
On a post about preparing nursery items, 🍼 can suggest a pregnancy without stating it outright. In comments about milk or feeding, the same emoji will usually be taken literally.
In a private chat, one bottle can feel like a playful announcement from a partner, sibling, or friend. Ask for clarification before treating it as confirmed news.

Family groups use 🍼 for pregnancy and baby-preparation updates because it conveys the idea without requiring a long explanation. Older relatives may still understand it only as an ordinary feeding bottle.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z users commonly treat 🍼 as a cute, understated way to announce that a baby is on the way. It feels softer than 👶 and less formal than a written announcement.
Millennials may use it in family chats to mean that bottles and other supplies are ready. Some still interpret it literally, especially outside an expecting announcement.

Gen X recipients are more likely to notice the literal feeding-bottle image first, particularly if the message is separated from a pregnancy post. They may need 👶 or 👣 to understand the intended hint.

warnings.title: Mistaking a hint for confirmation
warnings.description: 🍼 is a softer expecting signal, not proof that someone is pregnant. Use 👶 for a direct announcement or 👣 for the “tiny feet coming soon” version.

warnings.title: Hearing pregnancy news in every bottle
warnings.description: A practical conversation about milk, nursing, or packing baby supplies can make 🍼 completely literal. Send a bottle or milk emoji when that is the subject.

seoDescription: What does 🍼 mean? It often signals that baby bottles are ready—a soft hint that someone is expecting—or literally refers to infant feeding supplies.

longForm.overview:
🍼 entered Unicode Emoji 13.0 as a literal picture of a baby bottle, commonly shown with milk inside. That original meaning remains important: the image represents infant feeding and the practical objects associated with caring for a baby. It is not a gender symbol, and it does not by itself say whether a baby has been born.

Its newer conversational use came through baby-announcement language. Instead of writing out the news, people send 🍼 to suggest that the bottles are ready and a baby is coming. It is a softer hint than 👶, which plainly announces an expectation, and a playful variation on 👣, which evokes tiny feet. The best interpretation is “baby preparations are underway,” not necessarily a confirmed announcement. Surrounding words often settle the meaning: “the spare 🍼 is in the diaper bag” concerns infant care, while “tiny bottles are ready 🍼” is usually an expecting hint.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🍼 turns up in pregnancy reveals, nursery-preparation posts, and family chats where someone wants to share good news without making the message heavy. It commonly follows a nursery photo, a shopping update, or a list of baby supplies. On its own, it gives the recipient the “bottles are ready” idea and leaves room for a fuller explanation.

It also retains its practical meaning. Someone asking about milk, packing feeding supplies, or joining a baby shower may use 🍼 to identify the object directly. The surrounding words matter: “the spare 🍼 is in the diaper bag” is about infant care, while “tiny bottles are ready 🍼” is usually an expecting hint.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not treat 🍼 as a definite pregnancy announcement unless the sender has clearly confirmed one. It is intentionally gentle, but that can also make it ambiguous. If the news matters, pair it with 👶, 👣, a due date, or a sentence explaining what is happening. Those choices communicate the announcement more clearly without relying on a bottle image alone.

Avoid it when you only mean ordinary milk or infant-feeding equipment, because family members may hear a pregnancy hint. Conversely, do not use it to tease someone into announcing a pregnancy if that is not what you know. A specific 👶 or 👣 communicates the intended announcement more directly without turning the bottle into a claim.
longForm.howToReply:
If 🍼 appears in an expecting post, congratulate the sender and ask about the nursery, supplies, or due date. You can match the playful tone with 👶 or 👣, both of which belong to the same announcement vocabulary. When it arrives alone in a personal chat, a light clarification may work better than jumping to congratulations: “Bottles for a baby shower, or news? 🍼”

If it lands on content you shared, decide whether it matched your intention. A bottle emoji collected on a nursery post probably acknowledges the announcement, while one attached to a complaint may mean someone is joking that the situation needs extra care. Ask rather than overinterpret, especially if you are not close enough to assume the pregnancy context.

faqs.question: What does 🍼 mean when someone sends it?
faqs.answer: It often means “the baby bottles are ready,” a soft hint that someone is expecting. It can still be literal when the conversation is about feeding an infant.

faqs.question: Is 🍼 flirty?
faqs.answer: 🍼 has no inherent romantic meaning. In a dating chat, it may be part of a playful baby or pregnancy hint, but its meaning comes from the surrounding conversation.

faqs.question: What does 🍼 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it is commonly used as an indirect pregnancy announcement or a sign that baby preparations are underway. A caption with 👶 or a due date makes the message less ambiguous.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🍼 and 👶?
faqs.answer: 👶 directly announces that a baby is expected, while 🍼 suggests that baby preparations are underway. 🍼 is softer and can also be taken literally as a feeding bottle.

conversationExamples.message: he keeps talking about nursery colors and now he sends 🍼 lol
conversationExamples.interpretation: This looks like baby news rather than flirting, though the relationship context may make it more personal. Ask whether he is expecting or preparing for someone else.
The sender is probably offering a playful, indirect pregnancy announcement. Congratulate them or ask who they are telling first.

conversationExamples.message: the office baby shower table is covered in 🍼 and tiny shoes
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here the emoji refers to baby-shower decorations or supplies, not necessarily to a pregnancy involving the sender. Thank the organizer or offer to help.
This is a warm family announcement that the baby supplies are prepared. Respond with congratulations and curiosity about what they have set up.
The paired emojis form a playful expecting reveal, with 🍼 suggesting preparations and 👣 evoking the baby. Celebrate without demanding extra details.
